components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — meat and body parts, as in 脸 face, 肝 liver; 腥 is the smell of raw meat.
星 (xīng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 猩 xīng and 醒 xǐng.

example.hanzi: 这部电影的场面十分血腥。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de chǎngmiàn shífēn xuèxīng.
example.english: The scenes in this movie are extremely bloody.
example.fact: The Battle of the Somme in 1916 remains one of the bloodiest single battles in human history: on its first day alone, British forces suffered about 57,000 casualties, nearly 20,000 of them fatal, making it the deadliest single day in the history of the British Army.

examples.hanzi: 那个画面太血腥了，我不敢看。
examples.pinyin: Nàge huàmiàn tài xuèxīng le, wǒ bù gǎn kàn.
examples.english: That scene was too bloody; I didn't dare to look.

examples.hanzi: 这是一场血腥的战斗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì chǎng xuèxīng de zhàndòu.
examples.english: This was a bloody battle.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — two feet stepping upward: 登 is to climb or board, as in 登山 mountain-climbing.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound hint; 登 dēng also sounds out 灯 dēng and 凳 dèng.
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 那位歌手第一次登台就赢得了满场喝彩。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi gēshǒu dìyī cì dēngtái jiù yíngdé le mǎnchǎng hècǎi.
example.english: That singer won thunderous applause the very first time she took the stage.
example.fact: When a 13-year-old Michael Jackson took the stage with his brothers at Harlem's Apollo Theater amateur night in 1967, the group's energetic performance reportedly caused the audience to erupt so loudly that the show's host had trouble restoring order. Their win that night helped launch the Jackson 5's professional career just two years later.

examples.hanzi: 演员们明天晚上要登台表演。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnyuánmen míngtiān wǎnshang yào dēngtái biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: The actors will go on stage tomorrow night.

examples.hanzi: 他紧张得不敢登台唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnzhāng de bù gǎn dēngtái chànggē.
examples.english: He was too nervous to step on stage and sing.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.

example.hanzi: 我们每星期四都有一次团队会议。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měi Xīngqīsì dōu yǒu yī cì tuánduì huìyì.
example.english: We have a team meeting every Thursday.
example.fact: The English word 'Thursday' comes from 'Thor's day,' honoring the Norse god of thunder, a naming pattern the Anglo-Saxons borrowed when adapting the Roman calendar, which had named the same day after Jupiter, the Roman god associated with thunder and lightning.

examples.hanzi: 星期四下午我有空，我们见个面吧。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqīsì xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu kòng, wǒmen jiàn gè miàn ba.
examples.english: I'm free on Thursday afternoon; let's meet.

examples.hanzi: 今天是星期四，明天就是周五了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì xīngqīsì, míngtiān jiù shì zhōuwǔ le.
examples.english: Today is Thursday, so tomorrow is Friday.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.

example.hanzi: 电线短路时冒出了一串火花。
example.pinyin: Diànxiàn duǎnlù shí mào chū le yī chuàn huǒhuā.
example.english: A string of sparks shot out when the wire short-circuited.
example.fact: A single lightning bolt can heat the surrounding air to roughly 30,000 Kelvin, about five times hotter than the surface of the sun, all in a spark that typically lasts less than a millisecond. That rapid heating causes the air to expand explosively, producing the shockwave we hear as thunder.

examples.hanzi: 他们的讨论擦出了新的火花。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de tǎolùn cā chū le xīn de huǒhuā.
examples.english: Their discussion sparked new ideas.

examples.hanzi: 篝火里不断飞出火花。
examples.pinyin: Gōuhuǒ lǐ búduàn fēichū huǒhuā.
examples.english: Sparks kept flying out of the campfire.

components.note: 力 (strength) — marks effort and work, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 劳 is toil, labour.

example.hanzi: 他每天辛勤劳动。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān xīnqín láodòng.
example.english: He works hard every day.
example.fact: 劳 gives 劳动 (labour), 劳驾 ('excuse me, may I trouble you'), 劳累 (weary) and 功劳 (merit). 五一劳动节 is May Day.

examples.hanzi: 工人们辛勤劳动了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen xīnqín láodòng le yì zhěng tiān.
examples.english: The workers labored hard all day.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的帮忙，辛劳你了。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de bāngmáng, xīnláo nǐ le.
examples.english: Thanks for your help, I appreciate the effort.

components.note: 知 (zhī, know) — gives the sound (zhì is close) and the idea: knowing well is wisdom, as in 智慧.

example.hanzi: 他是一个很有智慧的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn yǒu zhìhuì de rén.
example.english: He is a very wise person.
example.fact: 智 is in 智慧 (wisdom), 智商 (IQ), 智能 (smart, as in 智能手机 'smartphone') and 人工智能 (artificial intelligence).

examples.hanzi: 这个手机很智能。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī hěn zhìnéng.
examples.english: This phone is very smart.

examples.hanzi: 你的聪明才智让我佩服。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de cōngmíng cáizhì ràng wǒ pèifú.
examples.english: I admire your intelligence and talent.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their relationships, as in 你, 信 trust, 借 borrow; a debt is what a person owes.
责 (zé) — loose sound hint (zhài vs zé), but 责 also means duty, which fits owing a debt; same part in 积 jī.

example.hanzi: 他还欠银行很多债。
example.pinyin: Tā hái qiàn yínháng hěn duō zhài.
example.english: He still owes the bank a lot of debt.
example.fact: 债 is colloquial in 欠债 (owe), 还债 (repay), and 债主 (creditor). 人情债 means a 'debt of gratitude'.

examples.hanzi: 他终于还清了所有的债务。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú huán qīng le suǒyǒu de zhàiwù.
examples.english: He finally paid off all his debts.

examples.hanzi: 欠债还钱是应该的。
examples.pinyin: Qiàn zhài huán qián shì yīnggāi de.
examples.english: Paying back what you owe is only right.

meanings: (of a device, connection, material etc) defective

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
良 (liáng) — good; as a part it sounds out 粮 liáng, 狼 láng, 浪 làng and 朗 lǎng.

example.hanzi: 长期熬夜会导致不良的健康后果。
example.pinyin: Chángqī áoyè huì dǎozhì bùliáng de jiànkāng hòuguǒ.
example.english: Long-term staying up late can lead to poor health consequences.
example.fact: Researchers at the University of California found that even a single night of significant sleep deprivation increases activity in the brain's amygdala, the region tied to emotional reactivity, while weakening its connection to the prefrontal cortex, which normally regulates that response. Chronic sleep loss has since been linked to measurable increases in the risk of heart disease, diabetes, and impaired immune function.

examples.hanzi: 这家店因为服务不良被客人投诉了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn yīnwèi fúwù bùliáng bèi kèrén tóusù le.
examples.english: This shop was complained about by customers for poor service.

examples.hanzi: 吃了不良食品可能会生病。
examples.pinyin: Chī le bùliáng shípǐn kěnéng huì shēngbìng.
examples.english: Eating bad food may make you sick.

meanings: variant of 座標|坐标[zuo4 biao1]

components.note: 土 (earth) — two people 从 sitting on the ground 土: to sit. Also in 座 zuò seat.
木 (wood) — 标 first meant the tip of a tree, hence a mark or target; wood radical as in 树 tree, 板 board.
票 (piào) is the sound in traditional 標; same series 漂 piāo and 飘 piāo; simplified 标 now shows 示.

example.hanzi: 飞行员输入了目的地的坐标。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán shūrù le mùdìdì de zuòbiāo.
example.english: The pilot entered the coordinates of the destination.
example.fact: The Cartesian coordinate system, which lets any point on a plane be located using just two numbers, was introduced by French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes in 1637. Legend holds he was inspired by watching a fly crawl across the ceiling near his bed and realizing he could describe its position using its distance from two perpendicular walls.

examples.hanzi: 请告诉我你所在位置的坐标。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ suǒzài wèizhi de zuòbiāo.
examples.english: Please tell me the coordinates of your location.

examples.hanzi: 这张图的横坐标表示时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng tú de héngzuòbiāo biǎoshì shíjiān.
examples.english: The horizontal axis of this chart represents time.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 腿 leg, 脸 face.
却 (què) is only a loose sound clue for jiǎo.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 他小心地看着脚下的路,以免摔倒。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎoxīn de kànzhe jiǎoxià de lù, yǐmiǎn shuāidǎo.
example.english: He carefully watched the path under his feet so as not to fall.
example.fact: A single hectare of healthy soil can contain several tonnes of living organisms — bacteria, fungi, insects, and worms — quietly working underfoot to recycle nutrients. Scientists estimate that just one teaspoon of healthy soil can hold up to a billion bacterial cells, far more organisms than there are humans on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 他站在悬崖边，脚下是深深的山谷。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài xuányá biān, jiǎoxià shì shēnshēn de shāngǔ.
examples.english: He stood at the cliff's edge, with a deep valley beneath his feet.

examples.hanzi: 小心脚下，地很滑。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn jiǎoxià, dì hěn huá.
examples.english: Watch your step, the floor is slippery.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑, 胖); 肤 is the skin.
夫 (fū) — same sound — 肤 is fū, like 夫; also in 皮肤.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 阳光会让人的肤色变深。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng huì ràng rén de fūsè biàn shēn.
example.english: Sunlight makes a person's skin color darken.
example.fact: Human skin color evolved largely as a balance between two competing pressures: darker skin, rich in the pigment melanin, protects against UV-related DNA damage nearer the equator, while lighter skin allows more UV light to penetrate for vitamin D synthesis at higher latitudes with weaker sunlight. Genetic studies suggest this trait can shift within a population in as few as 100 generations under strong selective pressure.

examples.hanzi: 她的肤色很白，一晒太阳就红。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fūsè hěn bái, yí shài tàiyáng jiù hóng.
examples.english: She has fair skin that turns red as soon as she is in the sun.

examples.hanzi: 不同肤色的孩子在一起玩。
examples.pinyin: Bùtóng fūsè de háizi zài yìqǐ wán.
examples.english: Children of different skin colors play together.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 医生给他开了一张处方。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā kāi le yī zhāng chǔfāng.
example.english: The doctor wrote him a prescription.
example.fact: The 'Rx' symbol used on medical prescriptions is widely believed to derive from the Latin word 'recipe,' meaning 'take,' though a popular but unproven legend traces it to the Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian protective symbol. The oldest known written prescriptions come from Mesopotamian clay tablets dating back over 4,000 years, listing plant- and mineral-based remedies for various ailments.

examples.hanzi: 这种药需要医生的处方才能买。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào xūyào yīshēng de chǔfāng cái néng mǎi.
examples.english: This medicine can only be bought with a doctor's prescription.

examples.hanzi: 药剂师按处方给我配了药。
examples.pinyin: Yàojìshī àn chǔfāng gěi wǒ pèi le yào.
examples.english: The pharmacist filled my medicine according to the prescription.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and herbs, as in 花, 草, 茶; 苏 originally named the perilla plant, and is also short for Jiangsu and Soviet (苏联).
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在饮料里加一点苏打水。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān zài yǐnliào lǐ jiā yīdiǎn sūdá shuǐ.
example.english: He likes to add a little soda water to his drinks.
example.fact: English scientist Joseph Priestley invented a method for infusing water with carbon dioxide in 1767, creating the first artificial carbonated water, several years before he became famous for helping discover oxygen. His invention laid the groundwork for the entire soft drink industry, though it took decades before entrepreneurs began selling flavored versions commercially.

examples.hanzi: 这瓶苏打水一点甜味也没有。
examples.pinyin: Zhè píng sūdǎshuǐ yìdiǎn tiánwèi yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: This bottle of soda water has no sweetness at all.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈用苏打粉清洗厨房。
examples.pinyin: Māma yòng sūdǎfěn qīngxǐ chúfáng.
examples.english: Mom cleans the kitchen with baking soda.

components.note: 龙 — a picture of a dragon, simplified from 龍. It also sounds out 聋 lóng, 笼 lóng and 拢 lǒng.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals, as in 蛇 snake, 蚊 mosquito.
下 (xià) is only a loose sound clue for xiā.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的龙虾非常新鲜。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de lóngxiā fēicháng xīnxiān.
example.english: This restaurant's lobster is very fresh.
example.fact: American lobsters can live for over 100 years and keep growing throughout their lives, molting their hard exoskeleton dozens of times along the way. Contrary to popular belief they are not biologically immortal — molting becomes more frequent and energetically costly with age, and the strain of shedding an old shell eventually kills them.

examples.hanzi: 我们点了一只大龙虾，大家一起吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diǎn le yì zhī dà lóngxiā, dàjiā yìqǐ chī.
examples.english: We ordered a big lobster for everyone to share.

examples.hanzi: 小龙虾是夏天夜市里的人气美食。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎolóngxiā shì xiàtiān yèshì lǐ de rénqì měishí.
examples.english: Crayfish is a popular treat at summer night markets.

components.note: 力 (strength) — marks effort and work, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 劳 is toil, labour.
马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑, 驶; 驾 is to harness a horse, then drive.
加 (jiā) — same sound, different tone — 驾 is jià; 加 also sounds out 架 jià.

example.hanzi: 劳驾,借过一下。
example.pinyin: Láojià, jiè guò yíxià.
example.english: Excuse me, let me get through.
example.fact: In the 1960s, American anthropologist Edward T. Hall coined the term 'personal space' after observing how much distance people from different cultures kept from one another during conversation. His research founded the field of proxemics, which studies how spatial behavior and comfort zones vary across cultures.

examples.hanzi: 劳驾，请问洗手间在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Láojià, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.hanzi: 劳驾你帮我拿一下那个包。
examples.pinyin: Láojià nǐ bāng wǒ ná yíxià nàge bāo.
examples.english: Could I trouble you to hand me that bag?

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
土 (earth) — levelling the ground, hence even; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
匀 (yún) gives a close sound and the idea of even; it also sounds out 钧 jūn.

example.hanzi: 这个班的平均成绩是八十五分。
example.pinyin: Zhège bān de píngjūn chéngjì shì bāshíwǔ fēn.
example.english: This class's average grade is 85 points.
example.fact: The commonly cited 'normal' human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1851 study by German physician Carl Wunderlich, who averaged readings from 25,000 patients. Later studies using modern digital thermometers put the true average closer to 36.6°C, suggesting average human body temperature may have also genuinely cooled over the past 150 years.

examples.hanzi: 我每天平均睡七个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān píngjūn shuì qī gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: I sleep an average of seven hours a day.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的平均气温是十五度。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de píngjūn qìwēn shì shíwǔ dù.
examples.english: The average temperature in this city is fifteen degrees.

components.note: 虍 (tiger head) — the top of 虎; it also appears in 虑 lǜ and 虐 nüè, but in 虚 the link to tigers is lost.
弓 (bow) — marks bows and bending, as in 弯, 引, 张, 强; 弱 doubles the shape and pairs with 强 strong.

example.hanzi: 手术后他的身体很虚弱。
example.pinyin: Shǒushù hòu tā de shēntǐ hěn xūruò.
example.english: After the surgery, his body was very weak.
example.fact: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station can lose up to 1-2% of their bone mass per month in microgravity, roughly ten times the rate seen in osteoporosis on Earth. Without gravity to work against, muscles and bones weaken quickly, which is why astronauts exercise about two hours a day to counteract the effect.

examples.hanzi: 他生了一场大病，身体很虚弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēng le yì chǎng dà bìng, shēntǐ hěn xūruò.
examples.english: He had a serious illness and his body is very weak.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的经济还很虚弱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì hái hěn xūruò.
examples.english: This country's economy is still fragile.

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 我们的目的地是长城。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de mùdìdì shì Chángchéng.
example.english: Our destination is the Great Wall.
example.fact: Point Nemo, in the South Pacific, is the location on Earth farthest from any land — over 2,600 km from the nearest coastline in every direction. Because it is so remote, space agencies use it as a 'spacecraft cemetery,' deliberately crashing decommissioned satellites and space station modules there to avoid populated areas.

examples.hanzi: 我们的目的地还有两公里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de mùdìdì hái yǒu liǎng gōnglǐ.
examples.english: Our destination is still two kilometers away.

examples.hanzi: 火车准时到达了目的地。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē zhǔnshí dàodá le mùdìdì.
examples.english: The train arrived at its destination on time.

meanings: to force sb to do sth

components.note: 力 (strength) — making an effort; also in 努 strive, 动 move.
免 (miǎn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 晚 wǎn and 娩 miǎn.
弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.

example.hanzi: 他勉强通过了考试。
example.pinyin: Tā miǎnqiǎng tōngguò le kǎoshì.
example.english: He barely passed the exam.
example.fact: Photosynthesis is famously inefficient: even highly productive crop plants convert only about 1-2% of the sunlight hitting their leaves into stored chemical energy, with most of the rest lost as heat or reflected away. Scientists are researching ways to genetically boost that efficiency to help increase crop yields as the global population grows.

examples.hanzi: 她勉强笑了笑，没有说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā miǎnqiǎng xiào le xiào, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
examples.english: She forced a smile and said nothing.

examples.hanzi: 这点钱勉强够我们吃一顿饭。
examples.pinyin: Zhè diǎn qián miǎnqiǎng gòu wǒmen chī yí dùn fàn.
examples.english: This little money barely covers a meal for us.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 项 first meant the neck.
工 (gōng) is only a loose sound hint for xiàng.

example.hanzi: 这项政策将从下个月开始实行。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè jiāng cóng xià ge yuè kāishǐ shíxíng.
example.english: This policy will take effect starting next month.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a stone stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, contains 282 laws covering trade, property, and family disputes. It is one of the oldest deciphered legal codes of significant length ever discovered, and offers a rare direct window into how an ancient society tried to formally regulate everyday life.

examples.hanzi: 这项工作需要两个人一起完成。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng gōngzuò xūyào liǎng gè rén yìqǐ wánchéng.
examples.english: This task needs two people to complete it together.

examples.hanzi: 他在这项比赛中得了第一名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhè xiàng bǐsài zhōng dé le dì-yī míng.
examples.english: He won first place in this competition.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — here the ice form of 氵 (water): 决 first meant to break a dam, so a decisive break.
夬 (guài) is a loose sound clue for jué; 夬 also sounds out 快 kuài and 块 kuài.
斗 (dipper) — a measuring dipper with a handle; as a radical it marks measuring: 料, 科, 斜. Also read dǒu (a measure) or dòu (to fight).

example.hanzi: 两位骑士为了荣誉进行了一场决斗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi qíshì wèile róngyù jìnxíng le yī chǎng juédòu.
example.english: The two knights fought a duel for honor.
example.fact: Dueling with pistols was legal or widely tolerated in much of Europe and the United States well into the 19th century. U.S. Vice President Aaron Burr famously killed former Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton in an 1804 duel in Weehawken, New Jersey — a death that helped turn American public opinion against the practice.

examples.hanzi: 他们在广场上约好了决斗。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài guǎngchǎng shàng yuēhǎo le juédòu.
examples.english: They agreed to have a duel in the square.

examples.hanzi: 古代有人用决斗来解决争端。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài yǒu rén yòng juédòu lái jiějué zhēngduān.
examples.english: In ancient times, some people settled disputes by dueling.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: achievement takes effort.
工 (gōng) gives the exact sound; 工 also means work.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and teaching, as in 说, 语, 读; 课 is a lesson.
果 (guǒ) hints at the sound: 课 kè is close to 颗 kē and 棵 kē, which share it.

example.hanzi: 我每天放学后先做功课。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān fàngxué hòu xiān zuò gōngkè.
example.english: Every day after school, I do my homework first.
example.fact: A large 2006 Duke University meta-analysis of homework research found only a weak link between homework and achievement in elementary school, with the correlation strengthening substantially by high school. This suggests the ideal amount of homework may depend heavily on a student's age and grade level rather than following one universal rule.

examples.hanzi: 你的功课做完了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de gōngkè zuò wán le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished your homework?

examples.hanzi: 她的功课很好，老师经常夸她。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngkè hěn hǎo, lǎoshī jīngcháng kuā tā.
examples.english: She does well in her schoolwork, and the teacher often praises her.

components.note: 彡 (hair strokes, decoration) — patterns and appearance: 形 shape, 影 shadow, 须 beard; 彩 is colorful decoration.
采 (cǎi) sounds exactly like 彩; also in 菜 cài and 踩 cǎi.
虫 (creature) — the ancients pictured the rainbow as a serpent in the sky; also in 蛇 snake.
工 (gōng) is a loose clue; 红 hóng shares it and sounds exactly like 虹.

example.hanzi: 雨后天空出现了一道美丽的彩虹。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu tiānkōng chūxiàn le yī dào měilì de cǎihóng.
example.english: After the rain, a beautiful rainbow appeared in the sky.
example.fact: A rainbow is not a fixed object hanging in the sky but a personal optical effect: each observer sees a slightly different rainbow, formed by their own unique cone of sunlight refracting through raindrops at just the right angle relative to their eyes. That is why no one can ever walk to the 'end' of a rainbow — it constantly repositions itself as the observer moves.

examples.hanzi: 彩虹有七种颜色。
examples.pinyin: Cǎihóng yǒu qī zhǒng yánsè.
examples.english: A rainbow has seven colors.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们指着天上的彩虹大叫起来。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zhǐzhe tiān shàng de cǎihóng dà jiào qǐlái.
examples.english: The children pointed at the rainbow in the sky and shouted.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is the mouth, as in 吃, 喝, 叫; 和 is harmony and speaking together.
禾 (hé) — same sound — 和 is hé, like 禾.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words, as in 说 say, 话 speech; 谐 is harmonious talk.
皆 (jiē) shares the rhyme -ie; only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 邻居之间应该和谐相处。
example.pinyin: Línjū zhījiān yīnggāi héxié xiāngchǔ.
example.english: Neighbors should live together harmoniously.
example.fact: Musical harmony traces back to the ancient Greek mathematician Pythagoras, who found around the 6th century BC that pleasing musical intervals correspond to simple numerical ratios between string lengths — a string exactly half as long, for instance, produces a note one octave higher. The discovery linked mathematics and music for the first time in recorded history.

examples.hanzi: 我希望我们的家庭永远和谐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng wǒmen de jiātíng yǒngyuǎn héxié.
examples.english: I hope our family stays harmonious forever.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌的旋律非常和谐。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ fēicháng héxié.
examples.english: The melody of this song is very harmonious.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 请把这次会议加入你的日程。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè cì huìyì jiārù nǐ de rìchéng.
example.english: Please add this meeting to your schedule.
example.fact: The 24-hour day and 60-minute hour used to structure schedules worldwide trace back to ancient Babylonian and Egyptian astronomy, which relied on a base-60 (sexagesimal) counting system. That same ancient system is also why a circle is divided into 360 degrees and a minute contains 60 seconds today.

examples.hanzi: 下周的日程已经排满了。
examples.pinyin: Xià zhōu de rìchéng yǐjīng pái mǎn le.
examples.english: Next week's schedule is already full.

examples.hanzi: 旅行日程是由导游安排的。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng rìchéng shì yóu dǎoyóu ānpái de.
examples.english: The travel itinerary was arranged by the tour guide.

meanings: (in reference to a person) role model

components.note: 木 (wood) — notices were posted on wooden boards; also in 树 tree, 桌 table.
旁 (páng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 膀 bǎng and 磅 bàng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 老师是学生的榜样。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī shì xuésheng de bǎngyàng.
example.english: Teachers are role models for students.
example.fact: Psychologist Albert Bandura's famous 1961 'Bobo doll' experiment showed that children readily imitate adult behavior they observe, even aggressive actions, simply from watching rather than being directly taught. The study became key early evidence for social learning theory and the powerful influence role models have on behavior.

examples.hanzi: 他是我们学习的好榜样。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen xuéxí de hǎo bǎngyàng.
examples.english: He is a great role model for us.

examples.hanzi: 父母要给孩子做个好榜样。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yào gěi háizi zuò gè hǎo bǎngyàng.
examples.english: Parents should set a good example for their children.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.

example.hanzi: 他在情报局工作了二十年。
example.pinyin: Tā zài qíngbàojú gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
example.english: He worked at the intelligence bureau for twenty years.
example.fact: The CIA's wartime predecessor, the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), was created in 1942 partly on the advice of British intelligence services already fighting Nazi Germany. Its work in sabotage, espionage, and code-breaking support during World War II laid much of the groundwork for the modern American intelligence community that followed.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家曾经在情报局当过翻译。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā céngjīng zài qíngbàojú dāng guo fānyì.
examples.english: This writer once worked as a translator at an intelligence agency.

examples.hanzi: 他的父亲在情报局负责分析资料。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fùqin zài qíngbàojú fùzé fēnxī zīliào.
examples.english: His father is in charge of analyzing data at the intelligence bureau.

components.note: 页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头 head, 顶 top, 题 title.
彡 (hair strokes) — hair or beard on the face, as in 影 shadow; together a beard, later "must" (必须).

example.hanzi: 乘客须系好安全带。
example.pinyin: Chéngkè xū jì hǎo ānquándài.
example.english: Passengers must fasten their seat belts.
example.fact: 须 is formal: 必须 (must), 须知 (notice), 无须 (no need). In a different sense, it means a beard: 胡须. Compare 需 (xū, to need).

examples.hanzi: 参加考试的人必须带身份证。
examples.pinyin: Cānjiā kǎoshì de rén bìxū dài shēnfènzhèng.
examples.english: Those taking the exam must bring ID.

examples.hanzi: 你无须担心，一切都准备好了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wúxū dānxīn, yíqiè dōu zhǔnbèi hǎo le.
examples.english: You need not worry, everything is ready.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.

example.hanzi: 他的年纪比我大。
example.pinyin: Tā de niánjì bǐ wǒ dà.
example.english: He is older than me.
example.fact: 纪 sits in 年纪 (age), 世纪 (century), 纪律 (discipline), 纪念 (commemorate) and 纪录片 (documentary). As a surname it is read Jǐ.

examples.hanzi: 他年纪不大，却很懂事。
examples.pinyin: Tā niánjì bú dà, què hěn dǒngshì.
examples.english: He is not old, but he is very sensible.

examples.hanzi: 学生们要遵守课堂纪律。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen yào zūnshǒu kètáng jìlǜ.
examples.english: Students must follow classroom discipline.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 她用心地照顾生病的父亲。
example.pinyin: Tā yòngxīn de zhàogù shēngbìng de fùqīn.
example.english: She attentively cared for her sick father.
example.fact: A landmark study published in JAMA in 2011 linked lower nurse-to-patient staffing ratios in hospitals to measurably reduced patient mortality across hundreds of facilities, underscoring how attentive, careful nursing care can directly affect recovery outcomes, not just comfort.

examples.hanzi: 他做每件事都很用心。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò měi jiàn shì dōu hěn yòngxīn.
examples.english: He puts his heart into everything he does.

examples.hanzi: 老师说我上课不够用心。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō wǒ shàngkè bú gòu yòngxīn.
examples.english: The teacher said I'm not attentive enough in class.

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你一直关照我。
example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ yīzhí guānzhào wǒ.
example.english: Thank you for always looking after me.
example.fact: Emperor penguin fathers look after their eggs almost single-handedly, incubating them on their feet under a warm skin fold called a brood pouch for about two months through the Antarctic winter, without eating, while the mothers travel to the sea to feed.

examples.hanzi: 新同事刚来，请大家多关照。
examples.pinyin: Xīn tóngshì gāng lái, qǐng dàjiā duō guānzhào.
examples.english: The new colleague just arrived, so please look after him.

examples.hanzi: 我已经跟经理关照过了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng gēn jīnglǐ guānzhào guo le.
examples.english: I've already notified the manager.

components.note: 气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.
自 (nose) — over 心 heart: breath comes through the nose from the heart, so rest, news.

example.hanzi: 春天的空气中弥漫着花的气息。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān de kōngqì zhōng mímàn zhe huā de qìxī.
example.english: In spring, the air is filled with the scent of flowers.
example.fact: A 2014 Rockefeller University study found that the human nose can distinguish over one trillion different odors, far exceeding earlier estimates of around 10,000. Each individual scent is detected through combinations of roughly 400 different types of olfactory receptors.

examples.hanzi: 这家咖啡店有一股浓浓的生活气息。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēidiàn yǒu yì gǔ nóngnóng de shēnghuó qìxī.
examples.english: This café has a strong feel of everyday life.

examples.hanzi: 森林里有泥土和青草的气息。
examples.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu nítǔ hé qīngcǎo de qìxī.
examples.english: The forest carries the scent of soil and fresh grass.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 此外,我们还需要准备一些饮料。
example.pinyin: Cǐwài, wǒmen hái xūyào zhǔnbèi yīxiē yǐnliào.
example.english: Besides, we also need to prepare some drinks.
example.fact: Mathematician Georg Cantor proved in the 1870s that infinity comes in different sizes: the infinite set of real numbers is strictly 'larger' than the infinite set of whole numbers, even though both sets go on forever. The discovery, once controversial among his peers, is now a foundational result in set theory.

examples.hanzi: 这家店东西很便宜，此外服务也很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn dōngxi hěn piányi, cǐwài fúwù yě hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This shop is cheap, and besides, the service is good too.

examples.hanzi: 除了英语，此外他还会说日语。
examples.pinyin: Chúle Yīngyǔ, cǐwài tā hái huì shuō Rìyǔ.
examples.english: Besides English, he can also speak Japanese.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — twisted threads, a tangle; also in 红 red, 级 level.
丩 (jiū, two strands twisted) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 叫 jiào and 收 shōu.
止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 老师纠正了我的发音错误。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiūzhèng le wǒ de fāyīn cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher corrected my pronunciation mistake.
example.fact: Modern eyeglasses trace back to 13th-century Italy, where craftsmen in Pisa ground convex glass lenses set in frames to help farsighted readers see fine print. Concave lenses for correcting nearsightedness followed roughly two centuries later, in the 15th century.

examples.hanzi: 请随时纠正我的语法错误。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng suíshí jiūzhèng wǒ de yǔfǎ cuòwù.
examples.english: Please correct my grammar mistakes at any time.

examples.hanzi: 他的坐姿不对，医生帮他纠正了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zuòzī bú duì, yīshēng bāng tā jiūzhèng le.
examples.english: His sitting posture was wrong, and the doctor corrected it.

components.note: 工 (tool, work) — originally a carpenter's square held in a hand — the same word as 矩; 巨 also sounds out 距 jù and 拒 jù.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 他从小城市男孩成长为国际巨星。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo chéngshì nánhái chéngzhǎng wéi guójì jùxīng.
example.english: He grew from a small-town boy into an international superstar.
example.fact: The red giant star Betelgeuse, in the constellation Orion, is roughly 700 times the diameter of the Sun — so large that if placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend past the orbit of Jupiter. Astronomers expect it to end its life in a supernova sometime within the next 100,000 years.

examples.hanzi: 这位歌坛巨星明晚在体育馆开演唱会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gētán jùxīng míngwǎn zài tǐyùguǎn kāi yǎnchànghuì.
examples.english: This singing superstar holds a concert at the stadium tomorrow night.

examples.hanzi: 她小时候的梦想就是成为巨星。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou de mèngxiǎng jiù shì chéngwéi jùxīng.
examples.english: Her childhood dream was to become a superstar.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — the left part, as in 话 speech. Memory aid: too many wagging tongues create chaos, hence 混乱.
乚 (hook) — the right-hand stroke and dictionary radical. 乱 is simplified from 亂; the stroke does not add meaning.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 别乱动这些实验器材。
example.pinyin: Bié luàndòng zhèxiē shíyàn qìcái.
example.english: Don't fiddle with this lab equipment.
example.fact: Brownian motion — the seemingly random jittering of tiny particles suspended in a fluid — was explained mathematically by Albert Einstein in a landmark 1905 paper, which showed the erratic movement was caused by countless collisions with individual water molecules. It provided some of the first direct physical evidence that atoms and molecules actually exist.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝总是在床上乱动，不肯睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao zǒngshì zài chuáng shàng luàn dòng, bù kěn shuìjiào.
examples.english: The baby keeps fidgeting in bed and won't sleep.

examples.hanzi: 请不要乱动桌上的文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào luàn dòng zhuō shàng de wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please don't mess with the documents on the desk.

components.note: 赤 (red) — two reds blazing together: glowing and brilliant.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 赫尔是英国东北部的一座港口城市。
example.pinyin: Hè'ěr shì Yīngguó dōngběibù de yī zuò gǎngkǒu chéngshì.
example.english: Hull is a port city in northeastern England.
example.fact: Kingston upon Hull was the birthplace of William Wilberforce, the British politician whose decades-long campaign in Parliament led to the Slave Trade Act of 1807, banning the slave trade throughout the British Empire.

examples.hanzi: 赫尔先生是一位有名的作家。
examples.pinyin: Hè'ěr xiānsheng shì yí wèi yǒumíng de zuòjiā.
examples.english: Mr. Hull is a famous writer.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友赫尔下个月要结婚了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou Hè'ěr xià gè yuè yào jiéhūn le.
examples.english: My friend Hull is getting married next month.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 他生来就有一副好嗓子。
example.pinyin: Tā shēnglái jiù yǒu yī fù hǎo sǎngzi.
example.english: He was born with a good voice.
example.fact: Human infants are born with a startle reflex called the Moro reflex, an automatic response to sudden movement or loud noise that makes them fling out their arms and legs. It is present from birth and normally fades by around four to six months of age as the nervous system matures.

examples.hanzi: 这孩子生来就很聪明。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi shēnglái jiù hěn cōngmíng.
examples.english: This child was born clever.

examples.hanzi: 没有人生来就会开车。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén shēnglái jiù huì kāichē.
examples.english: Nobody is born knowing how to drive.

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.
欠 (open mouth, owe) — marks wanting and owing, as in 歌, 欢, 欲; 款 is a sum owed or paid.

example.hanzi: 请仔细阅读合同的每一条款。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zǐxì yuèdú hétong de měi yī tiáokuǎn.
example.english: Please read every clause of the contract carefully.
example.fact: The U.S. Constitution's Second Amendment is only 27 words long, yet it has generated more litigation and legal debate than almost any other clause in American law — a reminder that a handful of words in a founding legal document can carry outsized and contested weight for centuries.

examples.hanzi: 合同里有一条款写得不太清楚。
examples.pinyin: Hétong lǐ yǒu yì tiáokuǎn xiě de bú tài qīngchu.
examples.english: One clause in the contract is not written very clearly.

examples.hanzi: 签字之前请先看清楚各项条款。
examples.pinyin: Qiānzì zhīqián qǐng xiān kàn qīngchu gè xiàng tiáokuǎn.
examples.english: Please read all the terms carefully before signing.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的教育制度正在改革。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jiàoyù zhìdù zhèngzài gǎigé.
example.english: This country's education system is being reformed.
example.fact: China's imperial civil service examination system, the keju, ran for roughly 1,300 years, from the Sui dynasty until it was abolished in 1905. It was one of history's earliest large-scale meritocratic institutions, letting men of relatively humble background reach high government office simply by passing rigorous written exams.

examples.hanzi: 学校有严格的考勤制度。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǒu yángé de kǎoqín zhìdù.
examples.english: The school has a strict attendance system.

examples.hanzi: 公司的新制度下个月开始执行。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī de xīn zhìdù xià gè yuè kāishǐ zhíxíng.
examples.english: The company's new system takes effect next month.

meanings: to get out of the way

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk, as in 说 say, 请 please.
上 (shàng) is only a stand-in with the same rhyme -ang; the traditional 讓 used 襄 xiāng, also in 嚷 rǎng and 壤 rǎng.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 请让开,救护车要过去。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ràngkāi, jiùhùchē yào guòqù.
example.english: Please step aside, an ambulance needs to get through.
example.fact: Ambulance sirens in many countries alternate between two tones because a moving vehicle's sound shifts pitch due to the Doppler effect. The familiar 'hi-lo' pattern was designed to stay audibly distinct and attention-grabbing even as a vehicle's speed and position relative to a listener keep changing.

examples.hanzi: 请让开一点，我要进去。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ràngkāi yìdiǎn, wǒ yào jìnqù.
examples.english: Please step aside a bit, I need to go in.

examples.hanzi: 你快让开，别挡着路。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kuài ràngkāi, bié dǎngzhe lù.
examples.english: Get out of the way and stop blocking the road.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — thread and rein; 纵 is to let loose, as in 红 red, 级 level.
从 (cóng) rhymes loosely with zòng.
火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起纵火案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ zònghuǒ àn.
example.english: The police are investigating this arson case.
example.fact: Fire investigators can often tell whether a fire was deliberately set by studying burn patterns. Accelerant-fueled arson fires tend to leave distinctive 'pour patterns' and unusually fast, intense burns, and lab techniques like gas chromatography can detect trace chemical residues, such as gasoline, left behind in the debris.

examples.hanzi: 有人纵火烧了那座仓库。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zònghuǒ shāo le nà zuò cāngkù.
examples.english: Someone set fire to that warehouse.

examples.hanzi: 纵火是严重的犯罪行为。
examples.pinyin: Zònghuǒ shì yánzhòng de fànzuì xíngwéi.
examples.english: Arson is a serious crime.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 这辆车花了十万元。
example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē huā le shíwàn yuán.
example.english: This car cost a hundred thousand yuan.
example.fact: The human body contains roughly 100,000 kilometers of blood vessels — arteries, veins, and capillaries combined — enough to circle the Earth about two and a half times, all packed into a body typically under two meters tall.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市大约有十万人口。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì dàyuē yǒu shíwàn rénkǒu.
examples.english: This city has a population of about a hundred thousand.

examples.hanzi: 他的视频有十万次播放。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shìpín yǒu shíwàn cì bòfàng.
examples.english: His video has a hundred thousand views.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a bay on the water; also in 河 river, 海 sea.
奥 (ào) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 懊 ào.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.

example.hanzi: 澳大利亚有很多独特的野生动物。
example.pinyin: Àodàlìyà yǒu hěnduō dútè de yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: Australia has many unique wild animals.
example.fact: Australia is the only continent occupied entirely by a single country, and roughly 80% of its mammal, reptile, and frog species occur nowhere else on Earth. That extreme uniqueness stems from millions of years of geographic isolation after Australia broke away from the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.

examples.hanzi: 我想去澳大利亚看袋鼠。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Àodàlìyà kàn dàishǔ.
examples.english: I want to go to Australia to see kangaroos.

examples.hanzi: 我的表姐在澳大利亚留学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de biǎojiě zài Àodàlìyà liúxué.
examples.english: My cousin is studying abroad in Australia.

components.note: 離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — a written record; also in 说 say, 话 speech.
普 (pǔ) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 他的要求实在太离谱了。
example.pinyin: Tā de yāoqiú shízài tài lípǔ le.
example.english: His request is really outrageous.
example.fact: Western five-line staff notation, still used by musicians worldwide, was standardized by the 11th century thanks largely to the Italian monk Guido of Arezzo, who also devised the 'do-re-mi' solfège syllables that helped singers learn unfamiliar melodies far more quickly than by ear alone.

examples.hanzi: 他说的话太离谱了，没人相信。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà tài lípǔ le, méi rén xiāngxìn.
examples.english: What he said was so outrageous that nobody believed it.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的价格贵得离谱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de jiàgé guì de lípǔ.
examples.english: The prices at this shop are ridiculously high.

components.note: 户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 他投资了不少房产。
example.pinyin: Tā tóuzī le bùshǎo fángchǎn.
example.english: He has invested in a lot of real estate.
example.fact: Antilia, a 27-story private home in Mumbai, is widely reported as the most expensive residential property ever built, with estimated values well over a billion dollars and a staff of around 600 needed to maintain it — illustrating just how far luxury real estate valuations can exceed those of ordinary office towers.

examples.hanzi: 这套房产是他父母留下来的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào fángchǎn shì tā fùmǔ liú xiàlái de.
examples.english: This property was left by his parents.

examples.hanzi: 买房产要先看清楚产权。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi fángchǎn yào xiān kàn qīngchu chǎnquán.
examples.english: When buying real estate, first check the title carefully.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — planning is done by talking things through; also 议 discuss, 论 discuss.
某 (mǒu) is a near sound match for móu; same part in 媒 méi and 煤 méi.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 他被指控犯有谋杀罪。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng fàn yǒu móushāzuì.
example.english: He was accused of committing murder.
example.fact: Forensic DNA fingerprinting was first used to help solve a murder case in 1986, when British geneticist Alec Jeffreys assisted police in identifying a killer in Leicestershire, England. It was the first time genetic evidence secured a criminal conviction, launching the modern era of DNA-based forensic science.

examples.hanzi: 法官判他谋杀罪成立。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān pàn tā móshāzuì chénglì.
examples.english: The judge found him guilty of murder.

examples.hanzi: 谋杀罪的刑罚非常重。
examples.pinyin: Móshāzuì de xíngfá fēicháng zhòng.
examples.english: The punishment for murder is very severe.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: 托 is to hold up with the hand.
乇 (tuō) gives the exact sound.
马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 托马斯是我的好朋友。
example.pinyin: Tuōmǎsī shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
example.english: Thomas is my good friend.
example.fact: The name Thomas comes from the Aramaic word te'oma, meaning 'twin,' and was borne by the apostle Thomas in the New Testament, often remembered as 'Doubting Thomas' for reportedly refusing to believe in Jesus's resurrection until he could see the physical evidence for himself.

examples.hanzi: 托马斯每天骑自行车上班。
examples.pinyin: Tuōmǎsī měi tiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.english: Thomas rides a bicycle to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 我想把这个消息告诉托马斯。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhège xiāoxi gàosu Tuōmǎsī.
examples.english: I want to tell this news to Thomas.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — mouth-watering mutton; with 次 (standing for drool) it is the usual picture of envy.
心 (heart, bottom form ⺗) — feelings; also in 想 think, 念 miss.
莫 (mò) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 墓 mù and 幕 mù.

example.hanzi: 我很羡慕她的好口才。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiànmù tā de hǎo kǒucái.
example.english: I really admire her eloquence.
example.fact: Psychologists distinguish 'benign envy,' which motivates people to work harder to attain what someone else has, from 'malicious envy,' which instead makes people wish to see the other person lose it. Research published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology in 2011 found the two types produce different behaviors and even different facial expressions.

examples.hanzi: 我羡慕你有这么多时间旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànmù nǐ yǒu zhème duō shíjiān lǚxíng.
examples.english: I envy you for having so much time to travel.

examples.hanzi: 大家都很羡慕他们的幸福生活。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn xiànmù tāmen de xìngfú shēnghuó.
examples.english: Everyone envies their happy life.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.
世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.
主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.

example.hanzi: 基督徒相信耶稣是救世主。
example.pinyin: Jīdūtú xiāngxìn Yēsū shì Jiùshìzhǔ.
example.english: Christians believe that Jesus is the Savior.
example.fact: The Christ the Redeemer statue overlooking Rio de Janeiro, completed in 1931, stands 30 meters tall atop Corcovado mountain and is built from reinforced concrete and soapstone. It was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in a global public poll in 2007.

examples.hanzi: 他们把这位医生看作是病人的救世主。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen bǎ zhè wèi yīshēng kànzuò shì bìngrén de jiùshìzhǔ.
examples.english: They regard this doctor as the savior of the patients.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的英雄是人民的救世主。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de yīngxióng shì rénmín de jiùshìzhǔ.
examples.english: The hero in the story is the people's savior.
